correctness.rationale: Schultz's Stiefel description identifies Hom(C5,Kn) with the unit tangent sphere bundle V_{n−1,2}, dimension 2n−5, so Gysin with tangent Euler class gives precisely the parity-dependent rational degrees. A D5 reflection induces (u,v)→(u,−v) in the known one-reflection model: it fixes base, has degree (−1)^(n−2) on fiber and top, while 5-fold rotations cannot act nontrivially on a one-dimensional rational line. An explicit maximal cell of color placements with colors 0,1 in pentagon positions 0 and 2 is fixed by the color transposition with two simplex reversals, so its manifold orientation sign is +1; conjugacy and generation show all S_n preserve orientation. The natural coordinate projection to the boundary of the n-color simplex is S_n-equivariant, and the Schultz regular neighborhood of the diagonal plus vanishing rational Euler class for odd n makes its pullback nonzero on H^{n−2}; the simplex boundary top class has color sign. Poincare duality transfers this sign to H_{n−3}. External tensor products and rational finite-group transfer give quotient invariants. I independently checked the explicit top cell at n=5 with two orientation reversals; inspected the source exact cell-Lefschetz algorithm testing n=4,5,6 and the cited primary Stiefel input. No full D5-equivariant homeomorphism is asserted.

value.rationale: The pentagon coloring manifold is a classical natural Hom complex whose simultaneous position/color relabelings encode unlabelled colorings. The nontrivial target sign sectors and clean odd/even rational quotient boundary provide an exact intrinsic equivariant invariant not visible from the previously known Stiefel homotopy type or a single reflection.

final_claim: For every n>=4 the rational homology representation of the pentagon graph-coloring manifold Hom(C5,Kn) under commuting position D5 and color relabeling S_n is an explicitly specified sum of one-dimensional characters: if n is even only H_{2n−5}=1⊗1; if n is odd H_{n−3}=epsilon⊗sgn, H_{n−2}=1⊗sgn and H_{2n−5}=epsilon⊗1, yielding a rational sphere homology quotient for even n and a rationally acyclic quotient for odd n.
limitations: Only rational ordinary homology representations for all n>=4 and rational quotient homology; no integrality, torsion, full-dihedral homeomorphism or quotient homotopy type.
